PC: Obtain sufficient history and physical exam findings to identify a post-operative hematoma.
Effectively release both the skin incision and deeper muscle layers to relieve hematoma pressure.
Reassess patient vitals and response to hematoma drainage
Ask for cardiac monitoring, pulse oximetry, and non-invasive BP monitors; Gather history from patient, family member, and ward nurse; Call for support from Anesthesia team.
Ask for appropriate tools and medications for either intubation or cricothyroidotomy.
MK: Recognize need for intubation or cricothyroidotomy in anticipation of delay
SBP: Make arrangements for definitive management with return to OR and notify consultant of situation.
Recognize that patient-centered care requires interprofessional teams consisting of various health professionals (nurses, anesthesiologists, surgeons, etc.) to maximize a positive patient outcome.
ICS: Show clear leadership during time of uncertainty and potential crisis.
Recognize and validate the family member(s) concerns and treat them with understanding and respect.
Ask family member to leave room
Identify themselves and their roles to patients, family members, and other health professionals.
PROF: Remain calm and professional in interactions with allied health professionals and other colleagues.
